narrative.intro: Brasfield and Gorrie received $416M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Brasfield and Gorrie won 16 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $26M. Obligations are down 5.8% year over year. Department of Homeland Security is the largest buyer of Brasfield and Gorrie, obligating $326M in FY2026 to date. Department of Defense is the second-largest buyer, obligating $59.6M, followed by General Services Administration at $21.1M, Department of Justice at $9.8M, and National Aeronautics and Space Administration at $200K. Brasfield and Gorrie recorded $416M in the Commercial and Institutional Building Construction market in FY2026 to date, and smaller amounts in Engineering Services and Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction. Historical obligations show Brasfield and Gorrie at $178M in FY21 and $154M in FY22, rising to $679M in FY23 and then falling to $587M in FY24 and $442M in FY25. The FY26 total is partial and fiscal year to date, so the $416M figure does not represent a full fiscal year total.

sections.heading: How has Brasfield and Gorrie’s federal business trended over time?
sections.body: Brasfield and Gorrie’s obligations rose from $178M in FY21 to $679M in FY23, then fell to $587M in FY24 and $442M in FY25. Brasfield and Gorrie obligated $416M in FY26 to date, and obligations are down 5.8% year over year.

sections.heading: Who are Brasfield and Gorrie’s biggest federal buyers and markets?
sections.body: Department of Homeland Security is the top buyer, obligating $326M to Brasfield and Gorrie in FY26 to date, followed by Department of Defense at $59.6M. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the largest market for Brasfield and Gorrie at $416M in FY26 to date, with additional obligations in Engineering Services and Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction.
